source: docs/desktop/spike_electron/results/t2.md (wave W0B, 2 October 2026, main hidden session, 10 accepted Tauri spike runs) and docs/desktop/baseline/backend_ready.md
shell: Tauri spike (D:\dev\spikes\tauri-shell, nq-shell.exe) with the fixture backend of the T2 harness
rule: 04 D5.1: each figure within 10% of the spike median or inside its min to max range

memHomeMB.what: whole-tree private working set at HOME, after 2.5 s idle

memHeavyMB.what: whole-tree private working set after the heavy set

homeReadyMs.what: launch to HOME ready (spawn to the nqt:home-ready mark)

backendReadyMs.what: real backend alone, process start to first 200 from /api/health; taken before D1 (lazy imports and the result cache), so a later figure is expected to be lower and is reported beside it, not gated

navStartAfterSpawnMs.what: spawn to the start of the HOME document (the spike milestones and the page navigation start)

readySinceNavMs.what: HOME document start to the nqt:home-ready mark

frameMs.what: HOME document start to the first HOME frame (nqt:home-frame)

note: The W0B run was taken before D2. Behind the session token the spike opens the launch page, which redeems a one-time code and leaves for the terminal, so the launch-to-ready figure carries one extra hop (about 25 ms on the run of 3 October). The breakdown shows where a difference sits: before the HOME document starts (process and window), or after (page and data).
